what_happened: A retry of the user's "we need better skills" request was written to fix only the reason the first attempt was rejected: formatting was not run automatically before the checks. The retry dropped the skill work itself and said it was "not retried here". Nothing re-queued the dropped skill work, so the user's request is no longer being worked on. A person noticed and logged it as an intervention.
cause: Athena builds a retry's reading around the rejection finding, not around the original request. It has no rule that a retry must keep the original goal and add the fix. It also has no link from a dropped part of a request to a follow-up item, and no check that every part of the original request is either carried or queued. A request can therefore leave the queue without anyone deciding it should.
prevention: Add a code check at retry and follow-up admission. It compares the new reading's deliverables with the original request's. Any original deliverable that is missing must either be carried into the retry or be automatically queued as its own linked item. A reading that drops the original goal without a queued follow-up is refused. A rejection fix may be added to the original goal but may not replace it.
proposed_request: When a rejected job is retried or followed up, the new reading must keep every deliverable of the original request and add the fix for the rejection. If a part is deferred, Athena must automatically queue it as a linked item at the original priority. Admission must refuse a retry that drops original deliverables without a queued follow-up. Show that a retry of a job rejected for a formatting failure still carries the original work, and that a deliberately dropped part appears in the queue as its own item. Also re-queue the dropped "we need better skills" request now.
